text:
Alex Chu: ACME just dropped their telemetry extract. Need a concrete commit proposal (reserved GPUs + autoscale rules) to include in SOW.
Meera Patel: paste the extract or key metrics?
Alex Chu: key: baseline ~150 RPS steady (mostly chat followups), short peaks to ~2.4k RPS lasting 2-7m, mean tokens/request ~130, 18% single-turn.
Caitlin Brooks: client asks: committed cost certainty + transparent overage billing for transient spikes.
Alex Chu: rough throughput: our medium gen profile is ~9k output tokens/sec per GPU for similar mix. Peak tokens/sec = (2400 * 130)/60 = 5200 tok/s -> ~0.58 GPUs.
Alex Chu: but must account for concurrency, KV cold starts, input variation. We size in whole GPUs.
Meera Patel: what margin do you recommend?
Alex Chu: I suggest two-tier approach: baseline coverage + burst buffer. Baseline tokens/sec = (150*130)/60 = 325 tok/s -> ~0.04 GPU. Reserve 1 GPU for redundancy and steady-state. Burst buffer for 99th spikes ~5200 tok/s -> ~0.58 -> add 1 GPU. So baseline pool = 2 GPUs.
Meera Patel: that feels tight for their SLA. Add safety multiplier?
Alex Chu: apply a variance multiplier of 1.7 (token variance + KV cold penalty) -> 2 * 1.7 = 3.4 -> round up to 4 GPUs reserved.
Samir Khan: could we present an autoscale-first alternative? They care about predictability but also want headroom for marketing spikes.
Alex Chu: recommend hybrid: commit 4 reserved GPUs (monthly predictable charge) + autoscale ceiling = 18 GPUs. Autoscale config: increment = 2 GPUs, cooldown = 45s, evaluation window = 30s. Allow short overage credit for spike windows <=7m to prevent immediate billing surprises.
Caitlin Brooks: commercial ask: produce two SOW options: Option A = 4-GPU commit + autoscale, Option B = 8-GPU commit no autoscale with deeper discount. I need the delta numbers to show finance.
Miguel Ortiz: ops note: enforce session affinity (sticky routing) to keep KV cache warm. Without affinity throughput drops and latency increases. Recommend session-affinity TTL = 10h and cache-warm grace = 20s. Fallback to quantized variant if cold starts persist.
Alex Chu: do we have a quantized model validated on ACME prompts?
Miguel Ortiz: we ran their eval earlier; quant7b gives ~1.7x throughput improvement and ~8-12% quality gap on their test set. Acceptable as a fallback.
Meera Patel: what latency SLOs can we commit to with the hybrid plan?
Miguel Ortiz: with KV sticky and 4 GPUs: p95 < 420ms steady. Under heavy spike, fallback to quantized keeps p95 < 700ms. Recommend explicit degrade policy: route >=95th percentile to quantized model instead of queueing.
Samir Khan: security: ACME requires VPC isolation + customer KMS + in-region-only log retention. Does that mandate Dedicated?
Alex Chu: yes. Hosted can do region affinity but cannot guarantee in-region-only log retention or customer-managed KMS currently. Dedicated (or Private) is required. Provisioning lead time for a dedicated pool is ~7-12 business days; add 2-4 weeks for on-prem/air-gapped.
Caitlin Brooks: action items for SOW: 1) Alex to publish line-item sizing calc and three-month cost scenarios for reserved 4 vs 8 GPUs. 2) Eng (Miguel + Meera) to finish perf runs for quantized fallback on ACME sample. 3) Sales/legal (Caitlin + Samir) to draft SOW options and note lead times. I'll assemble pricing sheet by EOD tomorrow.
Alex Chu: will attach calc and a simple cost sheet once I finish the numbers.
Meera Patel: if quantized quality delta <=12% on their eval, we push for hybrid commit.
Miguel Ortiz: running quick perf: `./perf_runner --model quant7b --concurrency 48 --input acme_samples.json` 0m run, will post results.
capacity-bot: autoscale policy suggestion created: min=4,max=18,step=2,cooldown=45s,window=30s :gear:
Samir Khan: security questionnaire note: ACME's legal insisted on in-region trace retention. We'll mark that as blocker until Dedicated confirmed.
Caitlin Brooks: for pricing disclosure: provide sample overage calc: if they exceed reserved capacity and autoscale consumes +12 GPUs for 5 hours in a month, show on-demand delta. I'll plug pricing once per-GPU rates are set.
Alex Chu: also propose a 2-week ramp window in contract where autoscale is enabled and we meter actual usage to fine-tune commit.
Meera Patel: agreed. Add a clause: one-time sizing review after ramp to adjust commit with 30 days notice.
Miguel Ortiz: posted preliminary perf: median latencies steady ~320ms p95 ~400ms on base model; quantized p95 ~560ms under high concurrency. Will share detailed logs.
Alex Chu: perfect. I'll upload the spreadsheet and draft SOW snippets here after lunch.
Caitlin Brooks: thanks everyone. I'll start SOW draft and include both options and the ramp clause.
capacity-bot: reminder: create ticket in sales->capacity labeled `acme-commit-scope` with due date 3 business days.
Alex Chu: closing loop, will update thread after docs uploaded.
Meera Patel: :thumbsup:
